title: ADA Title II digital-accessibility compliance programs for small Illinois local governments
product_service: Fixed-price WCAG 2.1 AA programs for municipalities, townships, park/library/fire/sanitary districts: site + document inventory, automated+manual audit, CMS fixes, PDF remediation (or archive strategy), accessibility policy/statement, staff training, quarterly monitoring retainer.
target_customer: Village/city administrators, clerks, IT/communications staff and district directors at Illinois units of local government with <50,000 population (deadline Apr 26, 2028) and 50k+ (Apr 26, 2027); Illinois has 6,930 local governments incl. 3,218 special districts [A, WS15-S003].
purchase_motivation: Federal ADA Title II rule compliance dates (Apr 26, 2027 / Apr 26, 2028) [A, WS15-S001]; litigation/complaint exposure; small entities lack in-house staff.
spending_evidence: DOJ estimates the one-year delay alone saves entities ~$395M/yr annualized (~$210M/yr to small entities), implying multi-billion compliance spending nationally [A, WS15-S001]. Illinois-specific spend: MISSING.
representative_operators: Level Access, Deque, TPGi (enterprise accessibility vendors; revenue not verified) [E]
CivicPlus/Revize/Granicus (government CMS vendors bundling accessibility) [E]
AudioEye/UserWay overlay vendors (overlays widely criticized as insufficient) [E]
revenue_mechanism: One-time program fee ($3k-$25k by entity size) plus monitoring/remediation retainer ($150-$1,000/mo) [E].
typical_transaction_value: $5k-$15k initial for a small village/district; $2k-$10k/yr retainer [E]
direct_costs: Auditor/remediator labor (US or offshore), testing tools licenses, PDF remediation labor, assistive-tech manual testing time.
contribution_profit_note: ~$3k-$8k contribution per small-entity program plus ~$1.5k-$6k/yr retainer contribution [E].
working_capital_note: Local governments pay net-30 to net-60 after board approval; deposits uncommon; low inventory.
sales_cycle: 1-6 months (board/council meeting cycles; small purchases under local bid thresholds can be approved by administrators) [E]
repeat_purchase: recurring-contract: monitoring retainer; content keeps changing so remediation never ends
acquisition_channels: Direct outreach to clerks/administrators using Census/IEPA/association lists
Illinois Municipal League, IAPD (park districts), library system conferences
Partnerships with municipal website vendors and IT MSPs
Free automated scan reports as door-opener
customer_accessibility: Good: all entities and their websites are public; small entities are reachable by email/phone; procurement is often informal below bid thresholds [E].
supplier_accessibility: Confirmed: testing tools (axe, WAVE, screen readers) are freely/commercially available; remediation labor hireable [E].
competitive_intensity: moderate-high: national vendors and CMS providers target governments; overlays sold cheaply; few Illinois-focused small-entity specialists observed [E].
entry_strategy: Productized fixed-fee packages for the long tail of special districts/townships that national vendors ignore; publish Illinois deadline guidance; bundle PDF archive strategy to reduce scope; offer certification-free but documented conformance reports.
licenses: None required; standard business registration and E&O insurance advisable [E]. No professional license applies to accessibility auditing.
regulatory_barriers: Demand depends on a rule DOJ says it may substantively revise [A, WS15-S001]; SBA Advocacy recommended withdrawal for small governments [C, WS15-S002].
operational_risks: Scope creep in legacy PDFs; quality failures if over-reliant on automated scans; government website platform lock-in.
financial_risks: Demand cliff if DOJ narrows/withdraws the rule for small entities; slow municipal payments.
geographic_constraints: Remote-deliverable; Illinois focus is a sales choice, nationally applicable.
founder_expertise: WCAG 2.1/2.2 techniques, assistive-tech testing, PDF/UA remediation; CPACC/WAS credentials optional.
staffing: Founder sells + audits first; hire 1-3 remediation specialists (or offshore partner) by month 6-12.
automation_potential: AI-assisted triage of scan results, alt-text drafting, PDF tagging suggestions, report generation; manual AT testing and judgment stay human.
delegation_potential: Good with SOPs: auditing and remediation are teachable roles; sales relationships transferable.
scalability: Can expand to other states' local governments and to K-12/universities; capped by regulatory demand durability.
expansion: Document remediation production (WS15-002), vendor ACRs (WS15-003), Title III private clients, website rebuilds.
roic_note: Asset-light: <$15k at risk; ROIC potentially >300% if demand materializes [E].
critical_assumptions: Small entities will buy before the 2028 date despite possible DOJ revision
Price points of $5k-$15k are acceptable to small districts
Manual audit + remediation can be delivered at 45%+ margin
unanswered_questions: What share of Illinois small entities have already contracted for compliance?
Will DOJ's announced NPRM narrow scope (e.g., K-12, small entities)?
Typical Illinois local bid thresholds for professional services
Actual price points paid by comparable municipalities (procurement awards)
failure_modes: Race to the bottom with overlays/cheap scans
Long municipal sales cycles drain founder time
score_rationale: feasibility 9: no license. ai 7: real productivity gains in remediation. resilience 4: demand rests on a rule already delayed and under reconsideration. fcf 4: small-entity tickets are low; ceiling likely ~$250k/yr.
preliminary_verdict: advance - best-fit regulation-driven B2G service for a tech founder, but must be validated against DOJ's pending substantive revision before committing.

title: Residential rooftop solar sales/origination (third-party-owned) under Illinois Shines after 25D expiry
product_service: Sales designee or Approved Vendor originating lease/PPA residential solar (+storage) contracts; installation subcontracted.
purchase_motivation: Illinois Shines REC incentives; electricity price increases [E]; 25D ended for expenditures after Dec 31, 2025 [A, WS15-S032] shifting market to TPO.
spending_evidence: PY2025-26: 27,568 small DG applications reviewed, 22,126 approved, 234.4 MW; financing mix 28% purchase, 32% lease, 40% PPA [A, WS15-S012].
representative_operators: Sunrun/TPO financiers; regional installers (not verified) [E]
revenue_mechanism: Commission per watt sold or per contract.
contribution_profit_note: $500-$2k per closed system after lead/rep costs [E].
working_capital_note: Commissions paid at milestones (install/PTO) weeks-months after sale; clawbacks.
sales_cycle: Weeks per homeowner; 2-6 months to commission
customer_accessibility: Moderate: homeowners reachable but heavily solicited.
supplier_accessibility: Confirmed: AVs register sales designees [A, WS15-S014].
entry_strategy: None compelling beyond local referral networks.
licenses: Designee registration; installer needs ICC DG installer certificate [A, WS15-S014]; home-solicitation rules.
regulatory_barriers: 995 complaints in PY25-26; restitution programs show consumer-harm history [A, WS15-S012]; federal 48E TPO deadlines (not verified).
roic_note: Low capital but high CAC risk [E].
critical_assumptions: TPO tax credit eligibility persists for 2026-2027 installs
unanswered_questions: Federal 48E/45Y TPO deadlines under P.L.119-21
PY2026-27 application trend after 25D
score_rationale: resilience 2: incentive cliffs; entry 2: extreme competition; consumer-protection scrutiny.

title: Commercial/municipal energy procurement brokerage (ICC-certified ABC)
product_service: Supplier RFPs and fixed-price contract placement for SMB/industrial electricity and gas; municipal aggregation consulting; bill auditing; renewals management.
target_customer: Small-mid commercial/industrial accounts, churches, schools, condo associations; municipalities running aggregation programs.
purchase_motivation: Illinois retail choice; capacity-driven price volatility (not verified this session); renewals every 12-36 months.
spending_evidence: ARES serve 83% (ComEd) / 87% (Ameren) of nonresidential load; 100 ARES; 514 municipal aggregation programs (2022) [A, WS15-S026]; ~1.12M residential ARES customers [A, WS15-S037]. Broker fee levels MISSING.
representative_operators: National and regional brokers/consultants (not verified) [E]
revenue_mechanism: Supplier-paid adder (mils/kWh) over contract term; consulting fees for aggregation.
working_capital_note: Monthly residuals paid by suppliers after customer pays; front-loaded sales cost.
customer_accessibility: Moderate: many buyers but heavily solicited.
competitive_intensity: extreme: mature market, most load already switched.
entry_strategy: Transparent flat-fee procurement and bill audit for mid-size accounts; capacity-cost education.
licenses: ICC ABC certification with bond; annual report due March 31 [A, WS15-S027].
financial_risks: Residuals stop if customer leaves supplier.
geographic_constraints: Illinois deregulated territories; extend to other states with licenses.
automation_potential: Bill ingestion, usage analysis, RFP automation.
critical_assumptions: Newcomer can win accounts against entrenched brokers
unanswered_questions: Typical broker adders in Illinois
ABC bond amount and fees
2025-2026 capacity price impact on commercial demand for procurement
score_rationale: entry 2: saturated mature market (83-87% already switched). roic 8: capital-light residuals.
preliminary_verdict: hold - structurally regulation-created and capital-light, but saturated; only with a specific wedge.

title: Utility energy-efficiency program trade ally: small-business lighting/controls/refrigeration retrofits
product_service: Turnkey retrofits (LED, controls, refrigeration EC motors, door gaskets) sold under ComEd/Ameren/Nicor small-business EE programs, with incentive paperwork handled; install by licensed electrician subcontractors.
target_customer: Small businesses, churches, nonprofits, multifamily common areas in Illinois utility territories.
purchase_motivation: CEJA-mandated utility EE programs fund large share of project costs (budget figures not verified); bill savings.
spending_evidence: MISSING - ComEd/Ameren EE budgets not fetched this session.
representative_operators: Program trade allies/lighting contractors (not verified) [E]
revenue_mechanism: Project price minus utility incentive paid by customer; incentive often assigned to contractor.
direct_costs: Materials, electrician labor, disposal, program admin.
working_capital_note: Materials + labor fronted; utility incentive paid 30-90 days post-completion [E].
customer_accessibility: Good: SMBs plentiful; utility programs drive leads.
competitive_intensity: high: many trade allies; LED retrofit market maturing.
entry_strategy: Non-lighting measures (refrigeration, controls) where saturation is lower.
licenses: Electrical work requires licensed electricians (Chicago electrical contractor license) - via subcontractors [E]; trade-ally enrollment.
regulatory_barriers: Program rule changes each plan cycle.
staffing: Sales + project coordinator; subs for install.
automation_potential: Audits and proposal generation via photo/AI.
expansion: HVAC controls, heat pumps, benchmarking clients.
critical_assumptions: 2026-2029 EE plans keep generous SMB incentives
unanswered_questions: ComEd/Ameren 2026-2029 SMB program budgets and incentive rates
CRGA EE provisions
score_rationale: feasibility 5: licensed electrician subs. resilience 5: program-cycle dependent.
preliminary_verdict: hold - real mandated spend, but evidence on current incentives missing and competition high.

title: Energy-code compliance testing (blower door/duct leakage) for new residential construction
product_service: Code-required air-leakage and duct-leakage testing, ventilation verification and compliance certificates for builders and HVAC contractors; optional HERS ratings.
target_customer: Production/custom home builders, multifamily developers, HVAC contractors in Chicagoland and Illinois.
purchase_motivation: Illinois Energy Conservation Code requires latest IECC edition [A, WS15-S036], which includes mandatory testing (testing-entity rules not verified); 45L credit end for new homes after mid-2026 (not verified) reduces HERS demand.
spending_evidence: MISSING (Illinois permit volumes and test prices not verified).
representative_operators: HERS rating firms, energy raters (not verified) [E]
direct_costs: Technician time, equipment (~$5k-$10k per kit), travel.
acquisition_channels: Municipal building departments' lists of approved testers
entry_strategy: Scheduling reliability and same-week reports for builders.
licenses: RESNET HERS/BPI or jurisdiction-approved tester credentials (weeks-months) [E].
critical_assumptions: Municipalities enforce testing provisions
unanswered_questions: Which IECC edition and testing-entity rules apply in 2026 Illinois
Permit volumes
preliminary_verdict: hold - mandated but low-ticket and cyclical.

title: Radon measurement & mitigation (IEMA-licensed) for real estate transactions, rentals, daycares and schools
product_service: Licensed continuous-monitor radon tests for home sales/rentals/childcare facilities; commercial/school testing; sub-slab depressurization mitigation systems; post-mitigation retests and annual system checks.
target_customer: Home buyers/sellers via realtors and home inspectors; landlords; licensed childcare providers; school districts; commercial owners.
purchase_motivation: Illinois Radon Awareness Act disclosure at sale and lessor/tenant provisions (pages exist; text not captured) [A, WS15-S023]; reported triennial daycare testing requirement (not verified); health risk.
spending_evidence: Licensed workforce small: 131 new/renewal license applicants in 2025 [A, WS15-S022]; test/mitigation volumes MISSING.
representative_operators: Local radon contractors and home-inspection firms (not verified) [E]
revenue_mechanism: Per-test fee; per-mitigation installed price; retest/maintenance add-ons.
direct_costs: Monitors (CRMs), fans/piping, labor, licensed-lab fees, vehicle.
customer_accessibility: Good: transaction flow via realtors; daycares listed publicly.
supplier_accessibility: Confirmed: equipment and fans available; labs listed by IEMA [A, WS15-S023].
entry_strategy: Fast-turnaround CRM testing with same-day reports; childcare/landlord recurring programs.
licenses: IEMA measurement and/or mitigation professional license: approved course + NRPP/NRSB professional exam + QA plan (weeks-months) [A, WS15-S021]; mitigation tags; insurance.
regulatory_barriers: Licensing; mechanical/electrical permits for fan circuits in some towns [E].
founder_expertise: Radon science, building diagnostics, licensing exams.
automation_potential: Scheduling, report automation; physical work stays human.
expansion: Vapor intrusion, indoor air quality, bundle with WS15-018/019 environmental inspections.
critical_assumptions: Mitigation attach rate is meaningful in Chicagoland
Realtor referral channel accessible to newcomer
unanswered_questions: Exact Illinois childcare radon testing requirement
Market test and mitigation prices
Share of Illinois homes above 4 pCi/L
failure_modes: Price competition from home inspectors bundling tests
score_rationale: cash 8: paid at service. feasibility 6: license in weeks-months. resilience 7: disclosure-driven and health-driven.
preliminary_verdict: advance - mandated/disclosure demand, attainable license, paid at service; ceiling moderate.
